title: A Modular, Responsive, and Accessible HPC Dashboard Built upon Open OnDemand
problem: HPC systems have high barriers to entry for non-expert users due to reliance on command-line tools; growing user community requires more accessible interfaces.
motivation: As HPC adoption expands beyond specialists, web-based interfaces reduce barriers and improve researcher accessibility.
method: They created a web-based dashboard—a visual control panel you access through your browser—built on Open OnDemand (a framework that brings supercomputer access to the web instead of requiring complex command-line tools). The dashboard displays key information through separate pages: announcements about the system, its current status, details about your computing jobs, and real-time resource usage, all designed to work well on any screen size (phones, tablets, desktops) and built with accessibility standards so non-experts can navigate them without special technical training.
key_novelty: The core innovation is making HPC system interfaces usable for non-experts by redesigning dashboard pages to be responsive (adaptable to any screen size), modular (each section works independently), and accessible to people without command-line experience.
contributions: Responsive design for diverse client devices
Streamlined access to announcements and system status
limitations: Abstract-only; lacks user studies, adoption metrics, or quantitative usability improvements
